samples.summary: Upstream-controlled text is now echoed into agent-consumed stderr with no sanitization of control/C1 characters
samples.evidence: `upstreamDetail` (formatter.ts:104-121) takes the response body's `message` (or the whole body when it is a string) straight from the network and embeds up to 500 characters of it into the CLI's error envelope, which is then printed by `outputError`/`upstreamErrorJson`. On the content/export paths this is new behaviour: before this change those sites emitted only `HTTP <status>` (see the removed `throw new Error(\`HTTP ${res.status}\`)` in commands/docs.ts, notes.ts, slides.ts). Vector: a compromised/hostile server, or an MITM if the user configured an `http://` server (`HttpClient.base`, client/http-client.ts:82-85, does not require TLS), returns `{"message": "<attacker text>"}` for any docs/notes/slides content or export request. That text lands verbatim on the stderr the README explicitly tells agents to parse and act on — a prompt-injection / log-injection channel into the calling agent. JSON.stringify escapes C0 controls (so classic ANSI ESC injection is blocked), but it does not escape C1 (U+0080–U+009F, e.g. CSI U+009B) or bidi/format characters, so terminals that honour 8-bit C1 in UTF-8 remain reachable. Hardening: strip non-printable/C1 code points and consider quoting the detail as an opaque field rather than free text.

samples.summary: Envelope pass-through has no size bound, so a hostile server can flood stderr despite MAX_UPSTREAM_MESSAGE
samples.evidence: `forwardUpstreamError` (formatter.ts:166-169) and `upstreamErrorJson` (formatter.ts:190) re-serialize `res.data` verbatim whenever `isErrorEnvelope` is true, i.e. whenever `error.code` happens to be a string. `isErrorEnvelope` (formatter.ts:76-85) validates nothing else: `error.message` and any sibling fields may be arbitrarily large or deeply nested. The 500-character `MAX_UPSTREAM_MESSAGE` cap, whose stated purpose is that 'an HTML page or a stack trace cannot flood the agent's stderr', therefore only applies to the non-envelope branch. Vector: a malicious or compromised backend answers any `docs/notes/slides content` request with `{"error":{"code":"X","message":"<10 MB>"}}` (or a megabyte-deep object) and the CLI writes it all to the agent's stderr, exhausting the consumer's buffer/context. Bounding the forwarded envelope (or at least its `message`) would make the two branches consistent.

samples.summary: Array `message` is joined before truncation, materializing an attacker-sized string first
samples.evidence: `upstreamDetail` (formatter.ts:109-113) calls `raw.filter(...).join('; ')` on the upstream `message` array and only afterwards slices to 500 characters. A hostile server returning a class-validator-shaped body with a very large array forces the CLI to build the full concatenation in memory before discarding it. The body is already resident after `res.json()`, so the amplification is bounded and this is hardening only, not an exploitable DoS.

samples.summary: No test or guard covers control-character / oversized upstream text in the new stderr path
samples.evidence: packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts exercises envelope vs. framework bodies, HTML pages, arrays and null, but has no case for a `message` containing terminal control sequences or for an oversized forwarded envelope, so the sanitisation gap in finding 1 and the unbounded pass-through in finding 2 are untested and would not regress-fail. I grepped the CLI source for any existing sanitiser before concluding none exists.
searchedFor: read packages/cli/test/upstream-error.test.ts hunk in the diff

finding.summary: Reviewer did not produce a valid verdict: review query hit a run limit: error_max_structured_output_retries after 26 turns — Failed to provide valid structured output after 5 attempts (raise the ceiling or simplify the task; retrying will not help)

verdict.reason: The finding is not a code claim — it is the review harness's own run-limit termination message, containing no file, line, or described vulnerability. scripts/agent/ask.mjs:281-285 defines `error_max_structured_output_retries` as one of LIMIT_SUBTYPES, i.e. an SDK result subtype meaning a sub-agent query hit a turns/budget/structured-output-retry ceiling before emitting a verdict; the comment at scripts/agent/ask.mjs:276-279 documents this same class of outcome. Its stated remedy ("raise the ceiling or simplify the task") targets review pipeline configuration, not repository code. Nothing in the Security lane is asserted: no authorization gate, secret, injection sink, crypto/signature check, SSRF, deserialization, or path-traversal claim, hence no attacker vector and no protected operation whose other call sites could be enumerated. I also confirmed every occurrence of the string in the tree is the harness's limit-classification logic, its tests, or notes about it — not injected content attempting to redirect the review. An infrastructure failure to produce a verdict warrants a re-run/re-budget of the review, not a blocking security defect on the merge gate.
